ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) part his hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the common misconception that hair parting is a definitive Sunnah by clarifying that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not part his hair, nor did the Prophets of old keep long hair. This narration highlights the distinction between cultural practices and religious tradition, emphasizing that simplicity in grooming was characteristic of the Prophets rather than elaborate styling. It serves to purify the understanding of Sunnah from later accretions of custom.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Amro Bin Sabit, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said, ‘They (people) are reporting that the parting (styling) is from the Sunnah’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the Sunnah?’ I said, ‘They are alleging that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> parted’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> did not part, nor did the Prophets<sup>as</sup> beforehand keep (long) hair’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Amr ibn Ibrahim from Khalaf ibn Hammad from ‘Amr ibn Thabit who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘They narrated that parting the hairs is of Sunnah. He (the Imam) said, ‘Of the Sunnahl’ I said, ‘They think that the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, parted his hairs.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The Holy Prophet did not part his hairs nor did the Prophets grow their hairs.’”
